name: Swisscom AG
executive_summary: Swisscom AG (SCMN.SW) screens as a buy on cash generation, dividend income, and risk-adjusted value rather than deep quality or moat metrics. The quantitative model flags a 75% composite score (sector-relative 70%), driven by an 8.2% FCF yield, 4.2% dividend yield, and a Neff PEGY of 0.06 despite reported earnings growth of −9.6%. The investment case rests on Switzerland’s quasi-monopoly telecom franchise, a CHF 26 per share dividend approved at the 2025 AGM, and rising free cash flow, set against a post‑Vodafone Italy balance sheet that is heavier, more leveraged, and still integrating. The central debate is whether enlarged scale and Italian exposure can stabilise earnings, or whether acquisition-related amortisation, higher interest costs, and competitive Italian pricing will keep reported profits under pressure even as operating cash flow holds up.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Swisscom offers a rare combination of defensive infrastructure economics and screen-visible income: four of four model families pass (cheapness, dividend, GARP, risk), with standout hits on FCF Yield, High Dividend Yield, Composite Value, Earnings Quality, and Neff PEGY. The business quality case is straightforward—dominant fixed and mobile networks in Switzerland, majority state ownership, and recurring subscription revenue—but the screen explicitly does not endorse quality or moat frameworks: Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Magic Formula, Graham Defensive, and Piotroski F-Score (6/9) all fail. That profile fits a “cash-rich incumbent at a reasonable price” thesis rather than a classic deep-value or quality compounder.

The valuation hook is cash, not headline P/E. At P/E 26.1 and P/B 2.9, the stock is not optically cheap on earnings or book, yet FCF of roughly CHF 3.0bn (Yahoo, 2025) against a market cap implied by the screen metrics supports an ~8.2% FCF yield, well above European telecom peers. The dividend policy is explicit and shareholder-friendly: CHF 26 per share was approved at the general meeting on 25 March 2026 (news manifest), up from the CHF 1.14bn cash dividend outflow seen in each of 2022–2025. ROE of 10.4% is modest but acceptable for a regulated utility-like asset base.

The buy case therefore ties screen output to business reality: stable Swiss cash flows fund dividends and fibre/5G capex, while the 2024 Vodafone Italy acquisition (CHF 7.37bn purchase of business per Yahoo cash-flow statement) adds revenue scale but depresses reported net income through higher depreciation, amortisation, and interest. A value investor can underwrite the name if they believe normalised FCF will persist and the dividend is structurally covered—accepting that reported EPS may lag for several years.
financial_review:
Primary regulatory filings: none available. The `filings_index.json` catalogue (regime: euro_filings) contains zero annual, interim, or other entries and zero body extracts under `filings/bodies/`. All figures below therefore fall back to `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo Finance); interim filing verification is not possible from primary sources. Cached Yahoo quarterly income for 2026-Q1 is noted where relevant but is secondary to the annual series.

Income statement trend (CHF, Yahoo annual):

| Metric | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|--------|------|------|------|------|
| Revenue | 11.05bn | 11.07bn | 11.02bn | 15.05bn |
| Operating income | 2.04bn | 2.21bn | 1.95bn | 1.93bn |
| Net income | 1.60bn | 1.71bn | 1.54bn | 1.27bn |
| Diluted EPS | 30.93 | 33.03 | 29.77 | 24.54 |
| EBITDA | 4.45bn | 4.62bn | 4.88bn | 6.62bn |

Swiss revenue was broadly flat through 2024; the step-change to CHF 15.05bn in 2025 reflects consolidation of Vodafone Italy. Reported net income has trended down since the 2023 peak (CHF 1.71bn → CHF 1.27bn in 2025, −26%), consistent with the screen’s −9.6% growth flag and the EPS compression from CHF 33.03 to CHF 24.54. Operating income has been broadly flat around CHF 1.9–2.2bn, suggesting the earnings decline is driven substantially by higher D&A (CHF 4.69bn in 2025 vs CHF 2.82bn in 2024) and financing costs rather than operating collapse.

Cash generation is the brighter line. Operating cash flow rose from CHF 3.88bn (2022) to CHF 6.01bn (2025), and free cash flow from CHF 1.59bn to CHF 3.00bn, even as capex increased to CHF 3.01bn. Cash dividends paid remained steady at CHF 1.14bn annually (2022–2025), implying comfortable FCF coverage in 2025 (~2.6×) but tighter net-income coverage (~1.1×). The approved CHF 26 per share dividend (~CHF 1.35bn on ~51.8m shares) would require confirmation against FY2025 distributable reserves from a primary annual report, which is unavailable.

Balance sheet (CHF, Yahoo, year-end):

| Metric | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|--------|------|------|------|
| Total assets | 24.81bn | 37.85bn | 36.02bn |
| Shareholders’ equity | 11.62bn | 12.15bn | 12.24bn |
| Total debt | 2.03bn | 3.97bn | 3.73bn |
| Goodwill + intangibles | 6.91bn | 12.65bn | 12.26bn |
| Tangible book value | 4.71bn | −0.49bn | −0.02bn |
| Working capital | −0.69bn | −1.19bn | −1.62bn |

The 2024 step-up in assets, goodwill (CHF 6.60bn), and debt aligns with the Vodafone Italy acquisition (CHF 7.37bn cash outflow for business purchase in 2024 investing activities). Tangible book turned negative in 2024 and remains near zero in 2025—a red flag for asset-heavy acquirers. Working capital is persistently negative and worsening (−CHF 1.62bn in 2025). Interest expense rose from CHF 131m (2023) to CHF 362m (2025), consistent with acquisition-related leverage.

Pension and provisions: non-current pension and post-retirement liabilities are modest (CHF 50m non-current; CHF 200m current in 2025 per Yahoo balance sheet). Long-term provisions of CHF 1.41bn suggest restructuring or network-related obligations, but without filing bodies the nature and timing of these provisions cannot be verified.

Interim / quarterly: no interim filings are indexed. Yahoo cached Q1 2026 data shows revenue CHF 3.61bn and net income CHF 332m (EPS CHF 6.41), which is broadly in line with a run-rate near the depressed 2025 annual profit level, but this is unaudited secondary data only.

Gaps: no annual report, half-year release, going-concern statement, covenant disclosure, or segment breakdown could be reviewed from primary sources. Any verify-before-trade workflow should treat the financial review as provisional pending Swiss/ESEF or company IR filing ingestion.
risks_and_flags:
Regulatory and structural: Swisscom operates in a regulated Swiss market with political oversight (majority Confederation ownership), which supports stability but can cap pricing and returns. Italian operations expose the group to a far more competitive, price-sensitive market—a strategic shift not captured by historical Swiss-only screens.

Financial and integration: Reported earnings are in decline; net income fell 18% from 2024 to 2025 (Yahoo). Goodwill of CHF 6.58bn and intangibles of CHF 5.68bn (2025) create impairment risk if Italian synergies disappoint. Tangible book value is effectively nil. Negative working capital (−CHF 1.62bn) and rising interest expense (CHF 362m) weaken the balance-sheet quality that the screen’s “risk” family partially offsets.

Screen-specific weaknesses: Failed models include Financial Health, Piotroski F-Score (6/9—ROA, current ratio, and gross margin not improving), Dividend Growth, Economic Moat, and Deep Value. The screen’s “new” signal (one week, 0% conviction) offers no timing confirmation.

Governance and pension: State control limits hostile scenarios but may constrain capital allocation flexibility. Pension liabilities appear manageable on Yahoo data, but without filing language on funding status or covenants, pension risk cannot be dismissed from primary evidence.

Competitive / operational: News reports TIM and Fastweb (Swisscom’s Italian unit) nearing a 5G network-sharing deal (Yahoo, 6 January 2026)—potentially positive for capex efficiency, but confirmation of economics is absent. Morgan Stanley reportedly downgraded the stock on revenue concerns (“Umsatzsorgen: Morgan Stanley stuft Swisscom-Aktie herab”, 11 June 2026, Investing.com Deutsch).

Filing gaps: No going-concern, contingency, or covenant text is available from `filings/bodies/`; these risks remain unverified at the primary-source level.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is voluminous but thin in substance: most headlines are templated German-language market commentary from AD HOC NEWS rather than investigative or regulatory reporting. Material items from the manifest include:

- **FY2025 results and dividend:** “Swisscom AG (SCMWY) Full Year 2025 Earnings Call Highlights: Dividend Boost and Strategic …” (Yahoo, 19 February 2026); “Earnings Update: Swisscom AG (VTX:SCMN) hat soeben ihre Jahresergebnisse veröffentlicht…” (simplywall.st, 15 February 2026). Dividend increase to CHF 26 approved at AGM (“Generalversammlung genehmigt höhere Dividende von CHF 26 pro Aktie”, MarketScreener Schweiz, 25 March 2026).
- **Vodafone Italy integration:** Earnings call summary references successful integration amid revenue challenges (Yahoo, 19 February 2026). Balance-sheet evidence of the CHF 7.37bn acquisition is in Yahoo cash-flow data, not independently confirmed here.
- **Italy network strategy:** “Telecom Italia, Fastweb eye 5G cost savings with Italy's network deal” (Yahoo, 6 January 2026)—potential capex-sharing with TIM under project “Prism”.
- **Analyst action:** Morgan Stanley downgrade on revenue concerns (Investing.com Deutsch, 11 June 2026).
- **Valuation debate:** “Ist es zu spät, Swisscom (SWX:SCMN) nach einer einjährigen Rallye von 27% zu berücksichtigen?” (simplywall.st, 17 May 2026)—reflects post-rally timing risk after strong multi-year returns.
- **Product / local ops:** “Swisscom blue TV X” launch (AD HOC NEWS, 29 June 2026); fibre cooperation in Kaltbrunn (Linth24, 13 March 2026)—operational colour only.

No material management-change or regulatory-enforcement headlines were identified in the manifest. News coverage should be treated as supplementary; primary filing ingestion remains the critical gap.
research_rationale: The quantitative buy signal is supported by strong FCF generation and a raised dividend, but primary filings are absent and post-acquisition earnings compression plus Italian integration risk prevent full confirmation of the screen’s buy case.
